drafts.task: Every quarter we review who has admin access. List everyone in the Entra ID admin groups, our admin tools and GitLab. Ask each person's manager in Teams whether they still need it. Remove GitLab access the manager says no to, raise a Jira ticket for the rest, and record the review on our Confluence access review page. It needs two approvers, one after the other.

answer.name: Quarterly admin access review
answer.purpose: Lists everyone with admin access across Entra ID, admin tools and GitLab, asks each person's manager if access is still needed, removes GitLab access that managers reject, and records the review in Jira and Confluence.
good_for: Run this quarter's admin access review
Check who still needs GitLab admin access and remove the rest
Ask managers to confirm admin access and log the results in Confluence

inputs.what: The GitLab group or project to review.

steps.say: Read the access review page in Confluence to find the current list and past review notes.
List the members of each Entra ID admin group.
List the accounts in each admin tool.
List who has access to the GitLab group or project, and at what level.
Combine the lists into one list. Show each person once, with every place they have access.
For each person, find their manager and ask in Teams whether they still need this access. Ask one manager at a time, and keep the answer for each person.
For each GitLab access the manager says no to, remove that access. Do this only after the removal has been approved.
For each other person, raise one Jira ticket that asks for a check of the admin access. Use the Jira project key from the inputs.
Record the review on the Confluence access review page. Include each person, where they have access, the manager's answer, and the action taken or the Jira ticket.
Post a short summary of the review in Teams for the team.

drafts.hoped: Reads the Confluence table, then GitHub. Jira ticket and page update each need approval. Asks for the Jira project.

answer.name: Software version checker
answer.purpose: Compares the software versions in the Confluence 'Software inventory' table with the newest GitHub releases, then raises Jira upgrade tickets for anything out of date and updates the inventory page.
good_for: Check our software inventory against the latest GitHub releases
Raise Jira upgrade tickets for software that is behind
Update the software inventory page with the latest versions

inputs.name: Inventory page
inputs.what: Title of the Confluence page that holds the software table

inputs.name: Jira project
inputs.what: Jira project key where upgrade tickets should be created

steps.say: Find the 'Software inventory' page in Confluence and read it, including its table.
Read the inventory table. Note each software name, its GitHub repository and the version we run.
For each software item, read its newest release on GitHub.
Compare our version with the newest release. Mark anything older as behind. Skip items with no GitHub repository and list them for the staff member.
Search Jira for an open upgrade ticket for each item that is behind, so no duplicates are made.
Ask the approver to confirm the list of upgrades before any ticket is created.
For each item that is behind and has no open ticket, create a Jira upgrade ticket that names the software, our version and the newest release.
Update the inventory table with the newest release numbers and a link to each new ticket.
Post a summary in Teams: what is up to date, what is behind, and which tickets were created.

Check whether a new version of a tool has come out and log it in Jira

inputs.what: The Jira project where the ticket should be created.

inputs.name: Last known release
inputs.what: The release version you already know about. New releases after this one trigger a ticket.

steps.say: Read the releases of the GitHub repository given as input.
Compare the releases with the last known release. Keep only the releases that are newer.
If there is no newer release, tell the staff member that nothing is new and stop.
If there is a newer release, search Jira to see if a ticket for that release already exists, so no duplicate is made.
If no ticket exists, ask the approver in Teams to confirm the new ticket. Show the release name, date and link.
After approval, create the Jira ticket in the given project. Put the release name, date, link and a short summary in the ticket.
Tell the staff member in Teams what release was found and the ticket number.
